subject: Business Models
title: Homejoy: The Leakage Problem
description: A short lesson to help you apply Homejoy: The Leakage Problem.

hook.text: Homejoy matched cleaners with homeowners. It grew to $35 million in revenue—then collapsed.

buildup.text: Customers loved their cleaners. After the first booking through Homejoy, they hired directly and skipped the platform.

discovery.text: Homejoy had no ongoing value. The match was its only service. Once made, the platform was unnecessary.

twist.text: Handy, a competitor, survived by offering insurance and payment processing—ongoing reasons to stay on-platform.

climax.text: Marketplaces die when their only value is the initial match. Ongoing value prevents disintermediation.

punchline.text: Match once, lose the customer forever. Without ongoing value, you're disposable.

quiz.question: Why did Homejoy fail?
options: Customers hired cleaners directly after the first match

details.summary: Homejoy built a marketplace for home cleaning services but collapsed because customers and cleaners quickly exchanged contact information and transacted directly, bypassing the platform after the initial match..
details.whyItMatters: Leakage is the existential threat for service marketplaces where the value delivered is the ongoing relationship, not each individual match..
takeaways: Customers and cleaners exchanged contacts to avoid marketplace fees after first match
Leakage destroyed repeat transaction revenue that the business model depended on
Service marketplaces must add ongoing value beyond initial buyer-seller matching

faq.question: Why couldn't Homejoy prevent customers and cleaners from going direct?
faq.answer: Home cleaning creates personal relationships through repeated intimate service. Customers and cleaners meet face-to-face regularly. Exchanging phone numbers is natural and easy. The marketplace fee provided no ongoing value after the initial match. There was no incentive to keep paying the platform.

faq.question: How do successful service marketplaces prevent leakage?
faq.answer: They add continuous value through payment processing, insurance coverage, scheduling tools, replacement guarantees, and quality monitoring. Thumbtack and TaskRabbit provide liability protection that off-platform hiring lacks..
